name: Yellowish Olive
lede: Yellowish Olive is a yellowish shade of [[olive|olive]], one of Robert Ridgway's working names built by the plain grammar of modifier plus base color.

sections.title: A modifier, not a new color
sections.body: Yellowish Olive joins the modifier *yellowish* to the base color [[olive]], named for the fruit's flesh and leaf [1][4]. Ridgway's 1912 plate XXX, hue 23-double-prime, sets it at lightness 49 with a moderate chroma of 24 [1][4]. The ISCC-NBS system calls the matching block, 106, 'light grayish olive,' a Delta-E of 7.4 from Ridgway's point [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[baiko-brown]] and [[kronberg-s-green]], at 3 and 3.6 ΔE [1][4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this shade, as photographed, in 8.97% of 23,781 paintings, 2,134 paintings, nearly one painting in eleven; within a single canvas it reads as a distinct area in 1,165 of them [3]. That ranks it more common than 91% of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1700s, found in 6.8% of that century's 3,449 paintings, 1.4 times the expected rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, by lightness rank, in 32% of its 1,165 appearances [3]. Peter Snayers is its most devoted painter, using it in 7 of his 16 works here, 6.3 times the baseline rate of the museums those paintings come from [3]. The earliest dated appearance is a painting from 916, the same 916 painting that opens the record for [[dark-citrine]], 996 years before the name's first documented record in 1912; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [3]. It shares canvases with [[vetiver-green]] and [[codium-fragile-seaweed]] more often than chance, lifts of 5.1 and 4.2 [3].
